newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF to mull tax changes to help land sales.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF to mull tax changes to help land sales.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that the government would continue to consider revisions to land-related taxes, in order to facilitate real estate sales and promote the effective use of land.

"Concerning land-holding taxes, we will continue to put the issue up for consideration, in order to facilitate land liquidity and promote the effective use of land," Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee.

Land-holding taxes were first introduced in 1992 with the aim of making it costly to own large tracts of land. The tax rate was halved to 0.15 percent in the current fiscal year that started last April in the course of the government's annual tax revisions.
Mitsuzuka also said that scrapping the securities transaction tax should be considered as part Japan's "big bang" financial deregulation plans.
He added that any revision of this tax should take into consideration how it compares with taxes on securities and tax systems in other countries.
"We (the government) must also deal with this issue, taking into account discussions among members of the tax panel, in parliament and public opinion."

Nobuaki Usui, director-general of the ministry's tax bureau, told the same parliamentary committee that he did not think the current weakness in Japan's stock market was linked to the issue of the securities transaction tax.
